## Loading and preprocessing the data
```{r loading data}
options(scipen = 999)
activity_raw <- read.csv("activity.csv")
```


## What is mean total number of steps taken per day?
```{r total steps}
library(tidyverse)
total_steps <- activity_raw %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(steps = sum(steps, na.rm= TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

total_steps %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=steps)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)

mean_steps <- mean(total_steps$steps)
med_steps <- median(total_steps$steps)
```

The daily mean number of steps is `r round(mean_steps)`, and the daily median number of steps is `r med_steps`

## What is the average daily activity pattern?

```{r daily activity}
daily_steps <-
  activity_raw %>%
  group_by(interval) %>%
  summarize(avg_steps = mean(steps, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

daily_steps %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = interval, y = avg_steps)) +
  geom_line()

max_interval <- daily_steps$interval[which.max(daily_steps$avg_steps)]
max_avg_steps <- daily_steps$avg_steps[which.max(daily_steps$avg_steps)]
```

The 5 minute interval with the most steps on average is `r max_interval` with `r max_avg_steps` steps.

## Imputing missing values

```{r missing values}
total_na_steps <- sum(is.na(activity_raw$steps))
mean_na_steps <- mean(is.na(activity_raw$steps))

# Imputing step:
# Attach the daily average steps per interval, select the imputed value if the 
# original is NA, and remove all working columns
activity_imputed <- activity_raw %>%
  left_join(daily_steps, by = "interval") %>%
  mutate(steps_new = coalesce(steps, avg_steps)) %>%
  select(steps = steps_new, date, interval)

total_steps_imputed <- activity_imputed %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(steps = sum(steps),
            .groups = "drop")

total_steps_imputed %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=steps)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)

mean_steps_imp <- mean(total_steps_imputed$steps)
med_steps_imp <- median(total_steps_imputed$steps)
```

There are a total of `r total_na_steps` (`r round(mean_na_steps*100)`%) intervals missing step data. After imputing the missing number of steps with the daily average for that interval, we see that the mean number of steps per day increases from `r round(mean_steps)` to `r round(mean_steps_imp)` (an increase of `r round(mean_steps_imp - mean_steps)`) and the median number of steps per day increases from `r round(med_steps)` to `r round(med_steps_imp)` (an increase of `r round(med_steps_imp - med_steps)`).

## Are there differences in activity patterns between weekdays and weekends?

```{r weekdays}
activity_imputed <- activity_imputed %>%
  mutate(weekend = weekdays(as.Date(date)) %in% c("Saturday", "Sunday")) %>% # Boolean TRUE if weekend day
  mutate(weekday = if_else(weekend, "weekend", "weekday")) %>%
  mutate(weekday = as.factor(weekday))

daily_steps_imp <-
  activity_imputed %>%
  group_by(interval, weekday) %>%
  summarize(avg_steps = mean(steps), # not using na.rm=TRUE because the data should have no NAs.
            .groups = "drop")

daily_steps_imp %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = interval, y = avg_steps)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(weekday))
```
